Workflow details

This workflow prepares ISIMIP 3b temperature data for use in therMizer. It involves processing temperature data (ocean_temp_array) and generating vertical_migration_array and exposure_array required by therMizer.

TherMizer Formatting: The R script Prep_TempRealms_therMizer.Rmd merged WOA and ISIMIP data, setting the WOA average as a baseline. Differences were calculated and concatenated into GFDL_ocean_temp_realm_array.dat.
Creating vertical_migration and exposure Arrays: These arrays were generated using SetUp_Realms.Rmd.
Output Files
ESS_vertical_migration_array.Rdata
ESS_exposure_array.csv
These files are the final inputs for therMizer.

# Create the vertical migration array and fill it
```{r}

# ============================================================
# REALMS = depth strata of the water column.
#
# `vertical_migration_array[realm, species, size]` is the PROPORTION OF TIME a
# species spends in each stratum, and it MUST SUM TO 1 across realms for each
# species. therMizer evaluates the thermal performance curve separately at each
# stratum's temperature, then weights by this array and SUMS over realms
# (`colSums` in therMizer:::scaled_temp_effect). Weights that do not sum to 1
# therefore multiply the thermal effect rather than apportioning it.
#
# TWO realms, matching the forcing. `Ocean_temp_by_Depth_1961_2100.csv` has
# columns `r0to50` and `r50to150`, and therMizer matches ocean_temp columns to
# realms BY POSITION, not by name, so the count and order must agree.
#
# The 18-realm vector below is the Hawaii longline therMizer scheme
# (Woodworth-Jefcoats; see Ortega-Cisneros et al. 2025, Earth's Future 13(2)
# e2024EF004826, where that model uses 18 depth ranges keyed to species'
# preferred depths). Retained for reference only. A previous version of this
# script used a 3-realm binary scheme that did not match the forcing and did
# not sum to 1; the weights below are recovered verbatim from the committed
# GFDL_ESS_vertical_migration_array.Rdata.
# ============================================================

#realm_names <- c("r0to20", "r0to50", "r0to85", "r0to100", "r0to150", "r0to200",  "r0to1200", "r50to150", "r50to200", "r50to300", "r100to200", "r100to250", "r100to400", "r150to600", "r200to400", "r200to980", "r250to500", "r400to1200")
realm_names <- c("r0to50", "r50to150")
species_names <- as.character(species_params(params)$species)
sizes <- params@w

# Time-at-temperature weights, one row per species, summing to 1 across realms.
vm_weights <- rbind(
  "Atlantic Cod"          = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Haddock"               = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "White Hake"            = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Red Hake"              = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Silver Hake"           = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Pollock"               = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Redfish Unseparated"   = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "American Plaice"       = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Yellowtail Flounder"   = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Witch Flounder"        = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Atlantic Herring"      = c(r0to50 = 1.0, r50to150 = 0.0),
  "Capelin"               = c(r0to50 = 1.0, r50to150 = 0.0),
  "Thorny Skate"          = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Winter Skate"          = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Spiny Dogfish"         = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Monkfish"              = c(r0to50 = 0.0, r50to150 = 1.0),
  "Sand Lance"            = c(r0to50 = 0.9, r50to150 = 0.1), ## they rarely go beyond 100meters
  "Longhorn Sculpin"      = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8),
  "Atlantic Halibut"      = c(r0to50 = 0.2, r50to150 = 0.8)
)

# Every model species must have weights, and every row must sum to 1.
stopifnot(setequal(rownames(vm_weights), species_names))
stopifnot(identical(colnames(vm_weights), realm_names))
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(vm_weights) - 1) < 1e-9))

# Create the vertical migration array and fill it. Weights are size-constant,
# which is what the committed array holds; make them size-varying here if a
# species' depth use is ever resolved by body size.
vertical_migration_array <- array(0, dim = (c(length(realm_names), length(species_names), length(sizes))), dimnames = list(realm = realm_names, sp = species_names, w = signif(sizes,3))) # realm x species x size

for (s in species_names) {
  for (r in realm_names) {
    vertical_migration_array[r, s, ] <- vm_weights[s, r]
  }
}

# Guard: the thermal effect is apportioned, not multiplied.
stopifnot(all(abs(apply(vertical_migration_array, c(2, 3), sum) - 1) < 1e-9))

```


# Construct exposure array
```{r}
exposure_array <- array(0, dim = (c(length(realm_names), length(species_names))), 
                        dimnames = list(realm = realm_names, sp = species_names)) # realm x species

for (r in seq(1,length(realm_names),1)) {
  for (s in seq(1,length(species_names),1)) {
    if (any(vertical_migration_array[r,s,] > 0)) {
      exposure_array[r,s] = 1
    }
  }
}
dimnames(exposure_array)
```


```{r}
save(vertical_migration_array, file = "Ess_Fishmip_data/GFDL_ESS_vertical_migration_array.Rdata")
write.csv(exposure_array, file = "Ess_Fishmip_data/GFDL_ESS_exposure_array.csv",row.names = TRUE)
exposure_array <- as.matrix(read.csv("Ess_Fishmip_data/GFDL_ESS_exposure_array.csv",row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))

```
